sections.label: Mandatory second week paternity leave
sections.summary: The proposed amendments make the second week of paternity leave mandatory to better support fathers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We want to better support fathers to achieve this through the proposed amendments.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Hence, we are making the second week of paternity leave mandatory.

sections.label: Amendment effective date and shared parental leave
sections.summary: The amendment is intended to take effect from 1 January 2017 for children born on or after that date, and Shared Parental Leave increases from one week to four weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: The amendment is intended to take effect from 1 January 2017 to benefit children born on or after that date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: We are also increasing Shared Parental Leave from one week to four weeks.

sections.label: Adoption leave increase
sections.summary: Adoption leave will be increased to 12 weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Tan Chuan-Jin)
sentences.text: Adoption leave will be increased to 12 weeks.

sections.label: Mandating second week of GPPL
sections.summary: The speaker recalls speaking for this in Parliament for six consecutive years and is delighted the Government will mandate the second week of Government-paid Paternity Leave from January next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In fact, I recall speaking for this in Parliament for six consecutive years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I am thus delighted that the Government has now decided to mandate the second week of Government-paid Paternity Leave (GPPL) to be effective from January next year.

sections.label: Shared parental leave increase welcomed
sections.summary: It is good news that shared parental leave has increased from one to four weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Page: 52 It is, indeed, good news that shared parental leave has increased from one to four weeks.

sections.label: Independent leave and unwed mothers
sections.summary: The speaker suggests considering independent leave for each parent and welcomes amendments extending maternity leave benefits to unwed mothers and unwed persons who wish to adopt.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Perhaps, the next step is to consider independent leave for each parent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: I also welcome the amendments to extend maternity leave benefits to unwed mothers and unwed persons who wish to adopt.

sections.label: Support for unwed mothers
sections.summary: Speaker asks if more can be done for single unwed mothers, including Baby Bonus Cash Gift and HDB housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Still, I am wondering if more can be done for this group of single unwed mothers with plans to improve other aspects of unwed mothers' lives, like entitling them to receive the $8,000 Baby Bonus Cash Gift, and allowing them to rent or, even better, own a roof over their heads from HDB.

sections.label: Unwed mothers and benefits
sections.summary: Unwed mothers do not qualify for Baby Bonus, cash quantum, housing or parenthood tax benefits, and the speaker hopes Government will consider them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: They are solely responsible for the welfare of their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We have not made moves in terms of Page: 54 the Baby Bonus, the cash quantum, and in terms of housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: While they have children, while they are parents, they do not qualify for parenthood tax benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: While we do not want to encourage any move towards single parenthood, I do not think many of them made the decision on the fly, saying that, "Hmm, how about being a single parent?" I hope the Government, although many of these are outside of the purview of MSF, will consider them for the sake of the children.

sections.label: Workplace childcare facilities
sections.summary: Speaker asks how many Ministries or agencies currently provide childcare facilities within their workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: One question would be: how many Ministries or agencies currently actually provide childcare facilities within the workplaces?

sections.label: Child well-being in policy
sections.summary: Speaker says putting the child's well-being at the centre of family social policy is key, and supports the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I believe that putting the well-being of the child at the centre of social policy affecting the family is the key to the balancing act.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I, therefore, support this Bill to equalise the various parental leave schemes for unwed and adoptive parents.

sections.label: Gig economy and term contracts
sections.summary: Speaker says the economy is changing to a gig economy and 11% of workers are on term contracts.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The economy is fast-changing to what has been termed as the gig economy and, according to MOM's Labour Force Report last year, 11% of our workers are employed on term contracts.

sections.label: Tracking employer guidelines
sections.summary: Speaker urges MSF to work with MOM to track whether employers follow guidelines and intervene when they do not.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the short term, I urge MSF to work with MOM to track whether employers are following the guidelines and to intervene when they are not, so that "encourage" will become "strongly encourage".

sections.label: Expand family nucleus definition
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to expand its definition of "family nucleus" to include unwed single parents.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For the sake of the children, I urge the Government to expand its definition of "family nucleus" to include unwed single parents.

sections.label: MSF reforms and housing
sections.summary: The speaker calls MSF's CDAC reforms laudable, supports the Bill, and hopes the Government next tackles the whole housing issue.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: MSF has made reforms that move in the same direction, as the previous and current amendments to CDAC show.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These are laudable moves and I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But the work is only beginning and the reforms need to be holistic.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I hope the Government would move next to tackle the whole housing issue.

sections.label: Foster Parents Scheme numbers
sections.summary: Over 5,000 children have benefited from MSF's Foster Parents Scheme, but against a target of 500 there are around 300 foster children and 250 foster parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Today, more than 5,000 children have benefited from MSF's Foster Parents Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But against MSF's current target of 500, we only have around 300 foster children and 250 foster parents.

sections.label: Adoptions dropped since 2014
sections.summary: In 2014, 352 children were adopted, a sharp drop from 732 a decade ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2014, 352 children were adopted, which is a sharp drop from 732 a decade ago.

sections.label: Overseas adoption cost rise
sections.summary: The cost of adopting overseas, usually through an agent, has gone up considerably, ranging from $25,000 to $50,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The net effect is that the cost of adopting overseas, usually through an agent, has gone up considerably.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I was told that the cost ranges from $25,000 to $50,000 to adopt from overseas.

sections.label: Grant to offset adoption cost
sections.summary: The speaker says a small grant to offset this cost, perhaps helping all but high-income couples, would be welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, a small grant to offset this cost, perhaps helping all but couples in high-income brackets, would be welcomed.

sections.label: Foster parent and family support
sections.summary: A foster parent is praised and the Government is asked to consider proposals to help two families and support every child.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: She is a wonderful foster parent well-loved by the children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: These two families which I have highlighted here – one bonded by blood, the other bonded by conviction, choice and love – can get more help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, I hope that the Government can examine the possibilities that I have proposed and add them to this excellent CDCA Bill in due course, because this small group of families deserves our full support, because every child in Singapore is precious.

sections.label: Termination and leave entitlement
sections.summary: Section 9(8), 12AA states employees terminated with just cause lose Adoptive, Government Paid Maternity and Paternity Leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In section 9(8), 12AA, it is stated that employees who are terminated with just cause cease to be entitled to Adoptive Leave, Government Paid Maternity Leave and Government Paid Paternity Leave.

sections.label: Overseas employment benefit calculation
sections.summary: It asks how benefits are calculated for a woman resident in Singapore who ceased overseas employment or self-employment at delivery.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How are the benefits calculated for a woman who was employed or self-employed overseas if at the time of delivery of her child the mentioned woman is a resident in Singapore and ceased to be employed or self-employed overseas?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the computation of claims, a weekly index is used limiting the claims to a maximum of six days whilst the self-employed, such as hawkers, operate seven days a week.

sections.label: Shared parental leave cases
sections.summary: It asks how many cases of shared parental leave between spouses have occurred since its introduction under section 12E.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Pertaining to section 12E, what is the number of cases of shared parental leave being shared between spouses since its introduction?

sections.label: Paternity leave consumption rate
sections.summary: The Minister is thanked and the Bill supported, but attention is urged on paternity leave use, with 40% of fathers using it in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With that, I thank the Minister for the changes and I support the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, I urge that we pay attention to the consumption rate of paternity leave as only 40% of fathers used their one-week paternity leave in 2015.

sections.label: Unwed fathers maternity leave
sections.summary: It asks whether unwed fathers can enjoy the same full 16 weeks maternity leave now given to unwed mothers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: While unwed mothers are now entitled to full maternity leave of 16 weeks, are there considerations made to allow unwed fathers to enjoy the same?

sections.label: Protection beyond maternity leave
sections.summary: Asks whether protection can be extended beyond pregnancy and maternity leave to give security to mothers returning to work after childbirth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Can the protection be extended beyond Page: 60 pregnancy and maternity leave period so as to give security and assurance to mothers who return to work after childbirth?

sections.label: Returnship Programme for women
sections.summary: Suggests a four-to-six-month Returnship Programme to match women jobseekers with employers, alongside CSP and PCP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Besides the Career Support Programme (CSP) and PCP, to give confidence to these women and also potential employers, I suggest the introduction of a Returnship Programme spanning four to six months to facilitate the matching of women jobseekers and employers.

sections.label: Baby First Step Grant relief
sections.summary: States that the Baby First Step Grant and dollar-for-dollar matching benefits introduced on 24 March 2016 give further financial relief to families.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: With the introduction of the Baby First Step Grant and dollar-for-dollar matching benefits that were introduced on 24 March 2016, this gives a further financial relief to all the families.

sections.label: Maximising CDA fund usage
sections.summary: Asks MSF to consider maximising CDA fund usage for low-income families, including disbursing funds for children's benefit and transferring unused funds to post-Secondary or Tertiary education.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: With this context and to further support some of these families, I would like to ask MSF to consider how and what can be done to maximise the usage of the CDA funds, especially for the low-income families.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: If required, MSF or even an appointed guardian can disburse and utilise the funds for the children's benefit instead of giving the cash amount directly to the families under their name.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
sentences.text: Second, to enable automatic transfer of any unused CDA funds for the child's post-Secondary or Tertiary education.

sections.label: Paternity and shared parental leave
sections.summary: Supports additional Government-Paid Paternity Leave and increased Shared Parental Leave, and asks for 2015 and 2016 take-up percentages and steps to increase them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With regard to this Bill, firstly, I firmly support the additional week of mandated Government-Paid Paternity Leave and the increment of Shared Parental Leave eligible to fathers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Minister had previously stated that in 2013, about 28% of fathers took the Government-Paid Paternity Leave; in 2014, it was about 36%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what the percentages are for 2015 and, to date, for 2016, and most importantly, what steps the Ministry will be taking to Page: 63 increase the percentage of fathers taking the paternity leave?

sections.label: Levelling field for unwed parents
sections.summary: States that the changes level the playing field for children born to unwed parents and reduce disadvantages they face from birth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: By introducing these changes, we are levelling the playing field for children born to unwed parents and reducing the disadvantages they face from birth.

sections.label: Gratitude for paternity leave amendments
sections.summary: A Member welcomes the Bill's amendments, saying they give fathers more time with their children and signal its importance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: On a more serious note, I am grateful for the amendments in this Bill, especially as a father, as it gives us more time to spend with our children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am grateful that this sends a strong signal about the importance of spending time with your children, and I am hopeful that, in the future, when asked about the time spent with your children, everyone will reply, "I am glad I did".

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Tomorrow they will be a little bigger than they are today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Study their faces, their little feet and pay attention.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It will be over before you know it".

sections.label: Second paternity week and shared leave
sections.summary: The passage states that legislating a second week of paternity leave and shared parental leave of up to four weeks meet such demand and change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Legislating a second week of paternity leave and allowing for shared parental leave of up to four weeks cater for such demand and change.

sections.label: Fathers' paternity leave usage rate
sections.summary: Only 40% of fathers used their one week of paid paternity leave last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Only 40% of our fathers used their one week of paid paternity leave last year.

sections.label: Flexible work and unwed mothers' leave
sections.summary: A Member asks about legislating flexible work for mothers and welcomes full Government-paid maternity leave for all qualifying mothers regardless of marital status.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: If the Government wants to help our young families more comprehensively, can we also legislate that mothers can enjoy the statutory right to ask for flexible working arrangements during the first year of childbirth? : Mdm Speaker, let me continue in English.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I am also very encouraged by the move to extend greater support for unwed mothers by extending full Government-paid maternity leave to all qualifying mothers, regardless of their marital status.

sections.label: Baby Bonus and unwed mothers
sections.summary: The passage states the Baby Bonus scheme is still not extended to children of unwed mothers, as Mr Seah Kian Peng mentioned.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: First, as my fellow Member of Parliament, Mr Seah Kian Peng, has mentioned, the Baby Bonus scheme is still not extended to children of unwed mothers.

sections.label: Unwed mothers excluded from HDB schemes
sections.summary: Unwed mothers and their child are not a complete family nucleus, so they are excluded from many HDB schemes and can buy flats only at 35 and above under the Singles Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Unwed mothers and their child are still not regarded as a complete "family nucleus" and they are thus excluded from many of HDB's public schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: They can only buy their HDB flats if they are 35 years old and above under the Singles Scheme.

sections.label: HDB flat for unwed mothers
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government could let unwed mothers buy an HDB flat before age 35, and calls the Bill a milestone in supporting families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Government reconsider this fundamental need for lodging as these unwed mothers are often younger, and allow a concession in consideration of their plight and circumstances to purchase a HDB flat even before the mother turns 35?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We can always and certainly should do more but, today, this Bill is an important marker and milestone of progress in supporting our families.

sections.label: Adoption leave versus maternity leave
sections.summary: Adoption leave rises from four to 12 weeks from July 2017, while natural mothers have 16 weeks, longer largely for recovery from childbirth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Mr Louis Ng asked why the length of maternity leave and adoption leave differs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are increasing adoption leave from four weeks to 12 weeks from July 2017.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This is to strengthen the support to adoptive parents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Natural mothers currently have 16 weeks of leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Maternity leave is longer by a month, largely because natural mothers need time to recover from childbirth.

sections.label: Foster parents' parenting responsibilities
sections.summary: The passage agrees it should be easier for foster parents to discharge parenting responsibilities, noting about 400 foster parents care for over 400 children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: I agree with Mr Kwek that we should make it easier for foster parents to discharge their parenting responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We have about 400 foster parents caring for over 400 children today.

sections.label: Benefits for stay-at-home mothers
sections.summary: Eligible stay-at-home mothers already enjoy all Marriage and Parenthood measures except employment-related ones like leave benefits, and receive Baby Bonus, CDA, MediSave Grant, levy concession and care subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Today, eligible stay-at-home mothers already enjoy all the measures under the Marriage and Parenthood package except, understandably, those related to employment, such as leave benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: They will get the Baby Bonus Cash Gift, the Child Development Account (CDA) benefits, MediSave Grant for newborns, Foreign Domestic Worker levy concession, and basic child and infant care subsidies.

sections.label: Maternity leave pay for self-employed
sections.summary: A self-employed person working seven days a week and taking full maternity leave continuously will be paid based on seven days a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: A self-employed person who works seven days a week and takes the full maternity leave continuously will be paid based on seven days a week.

sections.label: CDA First Step for low-income families
sections.summary: Because low-income families face more challenges saving into the CDA, the CDA First Step of $3,000 was introduced earlier this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are mindful that low-income families face more challenges in saving into the CDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This is why we have introduced the CDA First Step of $3,000 earlier this year.

sections.label: CDA co-savings and leave
sections.summary: Under the scheme, $50 saved in CDA yields $250 co-savings, and paternity and shared parental leave are mandated and extended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Under this scheme, if lower income parents saved $50 in CDA, OCBC would contribute $100 into the account.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: As the Government provides matching contribution of $150, the children will effectively receive co-savings of $250 in return for the $50 saved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The Government is mandating the second week of Paternity Leave from 1 January 2017 and extending Shared Parental Leave from one week to four weeks from 1 July 2017.

sections.label: Pro-family childcare facilities
sections.summary: 35 Ministries and Government agencies have childcare facilities within their buildings, supporting a pro-family and pro-children environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: I also agree with Mr Alex Yam on the importance of recreating a pro-family and pro-children environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: There are 35 Ministries and Government agencies with childcare facilities within their buildings.

sections.label: Fathers bonding through leave
sections.summary: With two weeks of mandatory paternity leave next year, more fathers are hoped to bond with children and use shared parental leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: When the two weeks of mandatory paternity leave kick in next year, we hope that more fathers will take the opportunity to actively bond with their children from the time they are born.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Like Mr Patrick Tay, I also hope more fathers will use the shared parental leave so that they can further bond with their children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: These leave enhancements are focused on the critical infant period.

sections.label: Paternity leave take-up increase
sections.summary: Paternity leave take-up rose 10%, from 38% to 42%, and the Minister is urged to examine reasons for low take-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: I have just one clarification for the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: I note the increase in the number of fathers who have taken up paternity leave – it is a 10% increase, from 38% to 42%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: I urge the Minister to look into the underlying reasons for the low take-up to get to the source.

sections.label: Reviewing scheme impediments
sections.summary: The Minister is urged to conduct further studies and review impediments so schemes get used and achieve desired outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: So, I urge the Minister to look seriously into this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: I think we would conduct further studies and review what exactly are the impediments and what we could do to help make sure that these schemes that we are putting in place actually get used and achieve the desired outcomes that we want.      .
